Let previous and next be the neighboring indices containing the same character, using -1 and n when a neighbor is absent. A substring containing the occurrence at p may start after previous through p, and may end from p through next-1. These choices are independent, giving (p-previous)*(next-p) valid substrings for that one occurrence.

A left-to-right scan does not know next immediately. Store the last two indices of each character; when its next occurrence arrives, the middle occurrence’s contribution becomes computable. After the scan, finalize the last occurrence of each character using n as its missing next boundary.

Summing occurrence contributions counts every unique-character event exactly once, even for equal substring text at different positions. Unique means frequency exactly one, so a substring containing two copies contributes nothing for that character.

concept.question: How many sections contain one occurrence but exclude its equal-letter neighbors?
intuition: Listing every section and counting its unique letters repeats enormous work. Instead, let each occurrence contribute to precisely the sections in which it is the only copy of its letter.

For an occurrence, its previous equal letter limits the left boundary and its next equal letter limits the right boundary. The number of valid sections is the number of left choices times the number of right choices. Finalize an occurrence when its next equal letter is discovered.
concept.observation: An occurrence is unique only between its neighboring equal-letter positions.
approach: Track the two latest positions of each letter.
When another copy appears, finalize the preceding copy’s boundary-choice product.
Use the text’s end boundary to finalize each last occurrence.
concept.correctness: A section makes an occurrence unique exactly when it includes that position, starts after the previous equal letter, and ends before the next equal letter. Left and right boundaries are independent, so their choice counts multiply. Every unique letter in every section belongs to exactly one such occurrence, making the contribution sum exact.
